reviews.summary: NEEDS_CHANGES. Blocking issue is the metric-naming conflict between the operator decision the reviewer was given (option A) and the tree (option B), which the reviewer explicitly declines to adjudicate and requires a team-lead ruling on. Second issue is tree instability during review, requiring a declared freeze plus fingerprint. Third is a downgraded nit on the determinism loop, already resolved before their capture. Substantively the reviewer CORRECTED the defect report's diagnosis and confirmed the writer's: production is deterministic on both cross-product axes and always was, with four independent lines of evidence -- snapshot diffs v1->v2, v2->v3 and v1->v3 each show exactly one differing file (policy_test.go), so no production file was touched; a test-only change cannot fix production nondeterminism once the expectation is deterministic, and 80/80 targeted, 60/60 full-package and 12/12 -race runs in separate processes with fresh map seeds show none; the failure message's 'chose prefill-a' is production picking the lowest ID per the documented contract while the varying value was `want`; and statically decide sorts BOTH axes via sortedByID (policy.go:224-225) with the strict c.J < best.J-1e-12 threshold, the only map iteration in production being Handler.Pick's `range profiles` guarded by len(profiles)==1 and verbatim from the approved focal arm. Two clarifications recorded: lowestIDDecodeEligible is the tokenization-decline fallback only and not the argmin tie-break, which the input conflated; and prefill-a IS the documented contract rather than an unproven tie-break, though the caution against mirroring production's ordering rule in a test lands usefully, making TestTieBreakIsDeterministicOnBothCrossProductAxes the better form since it asserts the concrete winner and verifies the tie is exact first. Recommendations accepted: replace t.Skipf with t.Fatalf in the decode-dominated tie subtest since a skip is invisible in a green run; record the D1 regime interaction (D1 can move the arm between prefill-sensitive and prefill-indifferent rather than shifting a threshold) in code next to the existing D1 paragraph, stating no direction is claimed. Confirmed the prefill-indifference regime is real and the writer's reading correct, and that the Policy race-coverage gap was real and would have been flagged. Resolved since Round 1: doc.go:56 now correctly names contract_test.go. Verified on their fingerprint: focal arm 25/25 byte-identical to a pre-round snapshot; the four exact copies still byte-identical modulo the package clause; all 17 retained function bodies in shared.go and all 5 structs in types.go byte-identical with nothing added; policy.go, picker.go, handler.go, config.go unchanged since the Round 1 read so the objective, strict-subset config and registration chain all still stand; build, vet, test and golangci-lint (0 issues) green with the fingerprint identical before and after.
